text.p: Italian bonds drew to a close a few basis points up on the day and dealers said Italian markets had held up relatively well compared with other bonds.
Btp futures started to droop into the red in later trade and the lira slithered to 986.75/7.25 per mark after trading around 981 earlier.

"It's been an overall good day for Btps," one broker at a house in London said, noting the spread over the benchmark 10-year Bund narrowed to 172 basis points from 189 on Wednesday. The July 2006 Btp ended three basis points up at 109.30 while the March future on LIFFE was 24 basis points down at 128.40.
The March future had forged a contract high this morning at 129.37, not far off the now-expired December future's record peak of 129.83 set earlier this week.

Traders said the late flop in the futures market was down to profit-taking on U.S. and other bond markets but they noted that nevertheless Btp futures were suffering less than some of their neighbours.

"It's because the market still expects a rate cut. Today's CPI was as good as expected and the market thinks the Bank of Italy will cut soon -- not necessarily this week but once the budget is approved in the upper house," a London broker said.
Dealers reckoned another factor making the central bank pause before easing was also stalled wage contract negotiations between metalworkers unions and employers.

The London broker said the central bank might wait until an wage agreement was reached before easing. The government will hold separate talks with both sides on Tuesday in efforts to broker an accord.

Final November consumer prices data came in exactly as expected at 2.6 percent year on year, following October's 3.0 percent growth rate, fuelling rate cut expectations, dealers said. --Charlotte Cooper, Milan bureau +392 66129507
